display.title: Episode 472: The Lost Letter, Chapter 2 (Yud-Aleph Nissan)
display.summary_short: On Yud-Aleph Nissan before Pesach: why children are the heart of the Seder, Shema with two young brothers, and the conclusion of The Lost Letter, as a ten-year-old letter from the Baal Shem Tov is finally delivered.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Yud-Aleph Nissan 5751, days before Pesach. Uncle Yossi explains that Pesach centers on children: Pharaoh's decree targeted Jewish boys, Hashem miraculously saved and nourished the babies, and at the Red Sea the children were the first to recognize Hashem and sing 'This is my G-d.' The Seder is built to make children ask questions, and when Moshiach comes, the children of Tzivos Hashem will lead the parade out of exile. After the Hakochainik march, two young brothers recite the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time concludes The Lost Letter: ten years after the Baal Shem Tov's passing, the now-penniless Reb Leib sells his heavy closet and finds the sealed letter beneath it. He brings it to Reb Sholom, who recognizes his Rebbe's seal, reads that Reb Leib has learned the value of a blessing, and is asked to set him back on his feet; the letter bears that very day's date. Uncle Yossi then marks the Rebbe's birthday on Yud-Aleph Nissan and wishes everyone a kosher and happy Pesach.
display.lesson: Value a blessing, especially from a tzaddik; Hashem gives special powers to those who serve Him truthfully. At the Seder, children should ask, because asking is how we learn.

date.note: 'Today is Yud-Aleph Nissan'; 11 Nissan fell on a Tuesday in 5751, and the show wishes a happy Pesach.

advisories.note: Pharaoh's decree to throw Jewish baby boys into the Nile, told with the miracle of their rescue.
A once-wealthy man must sell his belongings to feed his family.

privacy.note: Two brothers reciting the Shema are named in full.

sources_cited.note: The Seder begins with the children's questions.
Cited as the prophet Daniel: the clouds of heaven that will carry us to Eretz Yisroel.

segments.title: Pesach Is All About Children
segments.summary: The babies saved in Egypt, the children's song at the Red Sea, why the Seder is built around children's questions, and the children's parade when Moshiach comes.

segments.title: The Lost Letter, Chapter 2
segments.summary: Reb Leib finds the lost letter after ten years and delivers it to Reb Sholom, who learns from it that Reb Leib's troubles are over.
